title: Blood in urine
claims: If you think you have blood in your pee, you need to get it checked, even if there is only a small amount or you are not sure it is blood.
The NHS advises asking for an urgent GP appointment or getting help from NHS 111 if you have blood in your pee.
Blood in urine may be bright pink, red or dark brown.
Blood in your pee must be checked out because it can be a sign of cancer; cancer may be easier to treat if found early.
At the appointment a GP may ask for a urine sample or arrange a blood test, prescribe antibiotics if an infection is suspected, or refer to a specialist.
Beetroot, some new medicines, bleeding from the bottom, and vaginal or period bleeding can make urine look bloody; the page says do not self-diagnose.
The page lists urinary tract infection, kidney stones and enlarged prostate as possible causes, each with a distinct symptom pattern.
